title: Cannot clone repos: 'ERROR: Repository not found'
description: New engineer, SSH key added to GitHub, but `git clone git@github.com:larderly/stock-service.git` fails with 'Repository not found'. Teammates can clone the same repo.
resolution: The SSH key was not authorized for the larderly org's SSO. In GitHub → Settings → SSH and GPG keys, click 'Configure SSO' next to the key and authorize larderly. Cloning worked right after.

title: GitHub org invite expired
description: Started two weeks ago, was on leave in the first week, the GitHub invite link now says it expired.
resolution: Invites expire after 7 days. IT re-sent the invite from the Okta GitHub app; accepted the same day. If this happens, post in #it-helpdesk and ask for a re-invite.

title: pip install fails with 403 from packages.larderly.example
description: `pip install -r requirements.txt` in orders-service fails on larderly-common with HTTP 403 Forbidden. Worked last month.
resolution: Registry tokens expire every 30 days. Running `ladle auth login` refreshed ~/.pypirc and the install worked. We added a clearer error message to Ladle that suggests re-running the login.

title: Kafka container restarts in a loop with `ladle up`
description: On a new MacBook, the redpanda container keeps restarting, exit code 137. Stock service then fails to connect to localhost:9092.
resolution: Exit code 137 means the container was killed for using too much memory. Docker Desktop was set to the default 4 GB. Raised it to 8 GB in Settings → Resources and the stack came up. The local stack needs at least 6 GB.

title: Counter web app fails to start: 'Unsupported engine' for Node 18
description: Following the dev environment setup page, installed Node 18. Running `npm install` in counter-web prints 'Unsupported engine: wanted node >=20' and `npm run dev` fails with a Vite error.
resolution: Counter Web and Whisk moved to Node 20 in March when we upgraded Vite. Run `nvm install 20 && nvm use 20`; there is an `.nvmrc` in the repo, so `nvm use` alone picks the right version. The setup page still says Node 18 and needs updating.

title: `ladle seed` fails: relation "venues" does not exist
description: Fresh clone of stock-service, `ladle up` works, `ladle seed` crashes with psycopg error relation "venues" does not exist.
resolution: Migrations had not been applied to the new database. Ran `ladle migrate` and then `ladle seed`. Since Ladle 2.4, `ladle up` runs migrations automatically, so update Ladle with `brew upgrade ladle` / `scoop update ladle`.

title: Integration tests time out connecting to Postgres on WSL2
description: On Windows with WSL2, `ladle test --integration` times out connecting to Postgres. Unit tests pass.
resolution: The repo was cloned under /mnt/c/ (the Windows filesystem), which makes Docker volume mounts very slow. Moved the code to the WSL home directory (~/code) and the tests ran normally. Always keep code inside the WSL filesystem.

title: Autopilot creates no draft POs in local environment
description: Testing Autopilot locally: set a SKU below PAR in stock-service, but no draft purchase order shows up in orders-service.
resolution: Only stock-service was running. Autopilot lives in orders-service and listens to the stock.below_par event, so both services must be up: `ladle up --with orders-service`. Also check the `autopilot-enabled` flag is on for the demo venue in local LaunchDarkly settings.

title: PR blocked: 'migration requires Platform approval'
description: PR adding a column to purchase_orders has one approval from a code owner but the merge button is still blocked.
resolution: PRs that touch database migrations need a second approval from the Platform team (CODEOWNERS rule on /migrations). Requested a review from @larderly/platform and it was approved the same day.

title: Cannot see production logs in Datadog
description: Datadog shows dev and staging logs but nothing for env:prod.
resolution: Production log access is only granted after completing the 'Secure Development Basics' course. Completed it in the learning portal; access was added automatically the next morning.

title: Tailscale connected but pantry.larderly.example does not load
description: Tailscale says connected, but Pantry and the package registry time out in the browser.
resolution: The laptop was still using a custom DNS server configured by a home router app, which overrode Tailscale's MagicDNS. Enabled 'Use Tailscale DNS settings' in the Tailscale menu and everything resolved.

title: Whisk components render without styles in Counter
assignee: Mei Lin Tan (Tech Lead, Counter Web)
description: After linking a local Whisk build into counter-web, buttons and inputs show without any styling.
resolution: The Whisk CSS must be imported once in the app entry point: `import '@larderly/whisk/styles.css'` in main.tsx. When using a local build with `npm link`, also run `npm run build` in whisk first, since the styles are generated at build time.

title: Hotfix deployed on a Friday without release note
description: A hotfix went to production on Friday and support did not know what changed.
resolution: Reminder of the process: hotfixes can skip bake time and the no-Friday rule, but the release captain must post a note in #releases explaining what was fixed and why it could not wait. Added a checklist item to the hotfix PR template.

title: Kitchen app on Android emulator cannot reach local gateway
description: Running kitchen-mobile on the Android emulator, all API calls to http://localhost:8080 fail with network error.
resolution: Inside the Android emulator, localhost is the emulator itself. Use http://10.0.2.2:8080 instead; set API_URL=http://10.0.2.2:8080 in kitchen-mobile/.env.local. The iOS simulator can use localhost.

title: Docker Desktop asks for a paid subscription
description: Docker Desktop shows 'Sign in required, your organization requires a subscription'.
resolution: Sign in to Docker Desktop with the work Okta account, not a personal Docker Hub account. The licence is assigned automatically to work accounts.

title: Request: kubectl access to the staging cluster
description: Need to debug a pod in staging, how do I get kubectl access?
